hints: Draw an imaginary vertical line up from 6 kPa on the x-axis and see where it hits each of the two curves first.
Remember higher CO2 shifts the curve to the right, so saturation must fall. Calculate change as final value at 1.5 kPa minus starting value at 1.0 kPa.
walkthrough:
**Find the fixed oxygen partial pressure**

Go to $6 \text{ kPa}$ on the x-axis (partial pressure of oxygen). Move straight up until you meet both curves. This keeps oxygen constant while we compare the two CO2 conditions.

**Read off both saturation values**

On the upper curve (CO2 = $1.0 \text{ kPa}$), the y-value is about $70\%$. On the lower curve (CO2 = $1.5 \text{ kPa}$), the y-value is about $50\%$. Take your time reading the grid carefully.

**Calculate the change**

Change = final minus initial:
$$ \text{change} = 50\% - 70\% = -20\% $$
The negative sign shows a fall in saturation. This is the Bohr shift, more CO2 lowers haemoglobin affinity for oxygen so oxygen is released.

options.A: Too large a fall. Careful reading gives about 70% down to 50%, not a 26% drop.
options.B: Correct. Saturation falls from about 70% to about 50%, so change is -20%.
options.C: Wrong sign. Increasing CO2 shifts the curve right and lowers saturation, so the change must be negative, not +20%.
options.D: Incorrect reading. 46% is close to the final saturation value alone, not the change between the two curves.
